state: New WRITTEN all-variable candidate within the proposed one-normal bridge; UNREVIEWED. No diagnostic, selected physical q-value or held input.
finding: For normal A, diagonalize it with eigenvalues a_i. For any common site-2 basis V, write H_i=V(B+a_iI)†(B+a_iI)V†. If each H_i has offdiagonal support graph a disjoint union of paths (not necessarily the same paths or phases), then the f274 additive-compound modulus bound in that basis is EXACT: ρ(|K(H)|)=σ1(X)²+σ2(X)² and thus η equals the latter. Reason: H=⊕H_i; cross compound blocks have Perron value ρ(|H_i|)+ρ(|H_j|), while same-block values are ρ(|H_i^[2]|). A PSD Hermitian matrix with a path-forest graph can be independently permuted and diagonally phase-gauged so its offdiagonals are nonnegative; its two-particle wedge hopping cannot cross particles on a path, so its additive compound is also entrywise nonnegative. Hence both ρ values equal the corresponding true largest eigenvalue / top-two eigenvalue sum. Individual reordering/gauges are used only to evaluate invariant block radii, not as fictitious common physical bases.
large_concrete_subclass: If B is unitarily upper or lower bidiagonal in some basis, then B†B and B+B† (including complex linear combinations) are tridiagonal in that basis, so all H_i have a common path graph for every normal A, regardless of trace of individual blocks. This includes generic nonnormal, unitary-irreducible B, extending beyond normal pairs and f274's both-squares-nonnormal seed (A is normal). Since T2 is already supported when one factor is normal, this proves the stronger η≤2L for this class rather than merely citing T2 as certificate success.
remaining_gap: Arbitrary irreducible B need not be unitarily bidiagonalizable. No proof or refutation of η≤2L for every one-normal pair; no certificate necessity or global T2/T3/novelty claim. Main's f274 adopted scope, f198/f215 disposition and prior correction remain unchanged.
